function: Excluded (system), p. 9: TDVSR (BiLSTM + BasicVSR) restores CIR amplitudes over an area from sparse ray-traced CIRs (channel estimation/synthesis, area 2) on single-antenna links without RIS.
notes: Reason code 6 (system), shown on p. 9: "In each scenario, one transmitting antenna is deployed, and 256 × 256 receiving points with a height of 2 m from the ground are set". Each receiving point is a single antenna, p. 4: "each antenna elements has been considered as an ideal omni-directional antenna", and each CIR is a scalar, p. 4: "a deterministic complex scalar"; Fig. 2(a), p. 5, shows one transmitting antenna and receiving antennas 1-20 at separate positions. The receiving points are spaced 0.54 m by 0.35 m over an area of about 89.1 m by 139.3 m at 28 GHz (pp. 8-9), so they are separate single-antenna receivers of a radio map, not an antenna array; MIMO appears only as motivation (pp. 1-2). No RIS, and not an OTFS or NTN work. Codes 1-5 do not apply: a research article (IEEE TWC) whose learned TDVSR model (BiLSTM time decomposition + BasicVSR, trained on SBR ray tracing) estimates the CIRs at unmeasured locations, i.e. estimation/synthesis of the channel, area 2 (p. 2: "utilize the deep learning video super-resolution model to estimate the area channel information"). The title on p. 1 matches the DOI.
